description: PULP APB3 GPIO F5 behavior with two declared cause bits: INTSTATUS (0x24, ro, read_clears) bits 0 and 1 are the pin-0 and pin-1 rise causes the ISR reads. The source is the one real interrupt output; the vector is the status word's content, not a CPU vector.
notes: the F5 facts are the same device facts as configs/behaviors/pulp_gpio_cause_f5_pins.json; only the enable mask, the type word and the stimulus value differ, so the same PULP apb_gpio RTL raises both pins' status bits

GPIOEN(4)=0xffffffff enables the output, INTEN(24)=0x3 enables pins 0 and 1, INTTYPE_LOW(28)=0x5 gives pins 0 and 1 the 2'b01 rising-edge type (rtl/apb_gpio.sv:131-137), and PADOUT(12)=0x3 raises both pins in one write

INTSTATUS (0x24) is the profile's ro + read_clears status word (rtl/apb_gpio.sv:154/160 clears r_status when the word is read), so reading it both returns the two-bit cause and clears it; clear_writes stays empty because the device declares no acknowledge register
PADDIR(0)=0x3 must be written by a preceding F4 case so both pins are device-driven; the rise that raises the interrupt comes from the PADOUT write, not from the host driver

this file states device facts only: the executor still cross-checks them against configs/peripherals/pulp_gpio_causal_local/component_profile.json, and the declaration does not prove the RTL raises both bits (the real run does)
